newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta share prices down on blue chip selling.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta share prices down on blue chip selling.

text.p: Jakarta share prices ended down on blue chip selling despite a late buying surge as investors snapped up some medium-sized stocks and noodle maker Indofood, brokers said.

In late-afternoon trade, the Jakarta composite index fell to an intra-day low of 679.21 points on foreign selling of blue-chips Telkom, Semen Gresik and Sampoerna as well as Bank Negara Indonesia and Bank International Indonesia, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index closed 5.33 points, or 0.77 percent lower at 682.61 points. Losers led gainers by 87 to 45, with 63 counters unchanged.
Brokers attributed the weak tone in Jakarta market as being in line with generally weak regional markets.

"The Jakarta share index has risen rapidly since last November without any significant correction until February. I think this was a healthy correction," Mooto Murata, an economist with Jakarta-based Daiwa Securities, said.
He said weak corporate earnings in 1996, starting with cigarette maker Sampoerna and ending with Bank Negara Indonesia, had trigerred the recent selling wave which was needed by the market.

"The general election next May could also have become a factor, but it has already been counted into stock prices," he said, adding that foreign investors remained confident in the Indonesian economy ahead of the general election next May.
Total turnover was relatively low at 420.2 billion rupiah on a volume of 180 million shares.
Brokers said the news of an inter-bank rate cut by the central bank, which was expected give a boost to the weak market, appeared to have had no positive impact on the bourse.
On Wednesday, Bank Indonesia cut its key discount rate for short-term securities (SBPUs) by 50 basis points.
In late trade, investors snapped up Indofood, retailer Ramayana, hotel firm Jakarta International Hotel and marble producer Citatah which helped the index to inch up, brokers said.

Indofood was up 175 rupiah to 5,775 rupiah on 4.2 million shares after it announced that it lowered the price of its planned internal acquisitions to 1.55 trillion rupiah from the previous 1.75 trillion rupiah.
Retailer Ramayana Lestari Sentosa was also active on after reports of a block sale on Tuesday of about 20 million shares. Brokers believed it was part of a private placement by the company.
Telkom was off 75 rupiah to 4,000 rupiah on 1.8 million shares. Brokers said it was due to market speculation over Telkom's 1996 results which are scheduled to be announced on March 20.
